R5B-bear-atv-0002.name: By Gyllenspetz Creek
R5B-bear-atv-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5B-bear-atv-0002.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Talchako Mainline FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Burn from 2021 (fire VA1545), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 27 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Gyllenspetz Creek 110 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Stuie, about 21 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.22438, -126.01555, where the truck road ends (Talchako Mainline FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 2.0 km on unnamed roads and trails by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 30 m S, climb about 0 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-8, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-10, closures 2026-10-16.
